body.p: In the final Office Action', the Examiner rejected claims 1-19 and 21 under 35 U.S.C. § 102 as being anticipated by the video game "Golden Eye 007" (hereinafter Golden Eye) and Proximity Mine page on Golden Eye Wiki site (hereinafter Proximity Mine).
By this Amendment, Applicant amends claims 1, 10, and 19, cancels claims 17-18

without any prejudice or disclaimer of the subject matter thereof and adds new claims 22-23. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the as-filed application, for example, in para. [0053]-[0054] and [0096] of the specification. Upon entry of this Amendment, claims 1-16, 19, and 21-23 remain pending and under examination.
Applicant respectfully requests that the Office favorably reconsider and withdraw the rejections, and timely allow the pending claims for at least the reasons set forth below.
Applicant respectfully traverses the rejection of claims 1-19 and 21 under
35 U.S.C. § 102 as allegedly being anticipated by Golden Eye or Timed Mine. However, to expedite the prosecution of the present application, Applicant amends independent claims 1, 10, and 19.
Applicant respectfully submits that Golden Eye fails to teach or suggest, at least the following
the second virtual item being a virtual mine placed by an enemy virtual
controlling, in response to a use instruction detected by the computer
device and while the second virtual item is in the effective state, a target
virtual character to use an equipped first virtual item, the target virtual
character being controlled by a player and belonging to a first camp

different from the second camp, and the first virtual item being configured

as recited in amended claim 1 (emphasis added), and similar features in amended independent claims 10 and 19.

Golden Eye discloses a remote mine game where a player can throw a mine that can be detonated when contacted by a character. "Proximity Mines is a weapon that is one of three types of mines found in GoldenEye, the other two being timed mines and remote mines. Proximity mines detonate whenever a moving object is within their range, making them perfect for taking out patrolling guards but wasteful for stationary objects." (lSt para in Proximity Mine).

That is, Golden Eye suggests switching a single item (i.e., the mine) from disabled to enabled state based on game character, NOT temporality disabling a virtual mine placed by an enemy character based on its location relationship with another item used by a player belonging to a different camp. Further, detonating the mine in Golden Eye would be a one- time action with NO possibility of restoration after the mine is detonated. Thus, Golden Eye and Proximity Mine fails to teach or suggest, at least, "the second virtual item being a virtual mine placed by an enemy virtual character belonging to a second camp; . . . the target virtual character being controlled by a player and belonging to a first camp different from the second camp, the first virtual item being configured to temporarily disable an item belonging to a virtual mine type located within a first influence range of the first virtual item; displaying, in response to the first virtual item being deployed by the target virtual character and the second virtual item

being located within the first influence range of the first virtual item used by the target virtual character, that the second virtual item is switched from the effective state to an ineffective state," as recited in amended claim 1 (emphases added).

In view of the above, Golden Eye and Proximity Mine fails to disclose each and every element of amended claim 1, and thus claim 1 and its dependent claims are not anticipated by Golden Eye. Amended independent claims 10 and 19, although different in scope, recite elements similar to those of amended claim 1. For at least reasons similar to those discussed above in regard to the rejection of claim 1, independent claims 10 and 19, are not anticipated by Golden Eye and Proximity Mine either, as well as their dependent claims.
Accordingly, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the rejection under 35 U.S.C. § 102.

Newly added claims 22 and 23 are allowable at least by virtue of their dependence from an allowable base claim, and on the merits of their own subject matter that is not disclosed in or suggested by the cited reference.

In light of the above, Applicant respectfully requests Examiner's favorable consideration and timely allowance of all pending claims. If any issues may be resolved by telephone with the Applicant's representative, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the numbers shown.
Please grant any extensions of time required to enter this response and charge any additional required fees to Deposit Account 505213.
